questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: The step in the home management process that involves deciding in advance what needs to be done to achieve a family goal is called
options: organising
evaluating
planning
controlling
questions.explanation: Planning is the initial step in the management process, involving deciding in advance what actions are needed to achieve a desired goal.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: The step in the home management process that involves arranging resources and assigning tasks to carry out a plan is called
options: controlling
organising
planning
evaluating
questions.explanation: Organising arranges the necessary resources, people, and tasks in a logical structure needed to carry out a plan effectively.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: The step in the home management process that involves actually carrying out planned tasks is called
options: executing (implementing)
controlling
evaluating
planning
questions.explanation: Executing (implementing) is the stage where the planned and organised activities are actually put into action.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: The step in the home management process that involves monitoring activities and adjusting them as needed to stay on track is called
options: planning
evaluating
controlling
organising
questions.explanation: Controlling involves monitoring ongoing activities against the original plan, making adjustments as needed to keep things on track.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: The step in the home management process that involves assessing whether a goal was successfully achieved, and identifying lessons for future planning, is called
options: evaluating
controlling
organising
planning
questions.explanation: Evaluating reviews the outcome of a completed task or goal, assessing success and identifying lessons to improve future planning and execution.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Family resources that include time, energy, skills, intelligence, and attitude are classified as
options: material resources
human resources
financial resources only
community resources only
questions.explanation: Human resources encompass the personal attributes and capacities individuals bring to managing the home, such as time, energy, skills, and attitude.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Family resources that include money, property, and communal facilities are classified as
options: human resources
time resources only
attitude resources only
material resources
questions.explanation: Material resources include tangible assets such as money, property, equipment, and community facilities available to a family.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Time management in the home is important mainly because time is a resource that
options: has no effect on the achievement of family goals
can always be purchased in unlimited quantities
is identical in value for every task, regardless of priority
cannot be stored, replaced, or recovered once it has passed
questions.explanation: Time is a uniquely limited resource that, once passed, cannot be stored or recovered, making its careful management essential to achieving family goals.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A technique used to reduce unnecessary effort and time spent on household tasks, often by rearranging tools or combining steps, is called
options: work simplification
financial planning
ergonomics only
fatigue management only
questions.explanation: Work simplification involves analysing and streamlining household tasks to reduce wasted time, effort, and motion.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: The study of designing tasks, tools, and environments to fit the physical capabilities of the person doing the work is called
options: fatigue management only
work simplification only
budgeting
ergonomics
questions.explanation: Ergonomics focuses on designing tasks and equipment to suit the physical needs and capabilities of the person performing them, reducing strain and injury risk.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Managing the onset of tiredness during household tasks, such as through proper posture and scheduled breaks, is called
options: work simplification only
fatigue management
budgeting
ergonomics only
questions.explanation: Fatigue management involves strategies such as proper posture, task rotation, and scheduled rest breaks to reduce and manage tiredness during work.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A schedule that allocates time appropriately across work, rest, and leisure activities throughout the day is called a
options: balanced daily work schedule
family budget
consumer report
house plan
questions.explanation: A balanced daily work schedule allocates appropriate time to work, rest, and leisure, helping to prevent overwork and burnout.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Family income received directly in the form of wages, salaries, or business profits is classified as
options: indirect income
gross income only
direct income
net income only
questions.explanation: Direct income refers to money received directly, such as wages and salaries, as opposed to indirect income received in other forms, such as benefits.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Family income received in forms other than direct money payments, such as free housing or subsidised meals, is classified as
options: gross income only
indirect income
net income only
direct income
questions.explanation: Indirect income includes non-cash benefits, such as free accommodation or subsidised services, that contribute to a family's overall economic wellbeing.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A family's total income before any deductions, such as taxes, are made is called its
options: gross income
net income
disposable income only
indirect income only
questions.explanation: Gross income represents total earnings before any deductions, such as taxes or other withholdings, are subtracted.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A family's income remaining after all necessary deductions, such as taxes, have been subtracted is called its
options: direct income only
net income
gross income
indirect income only
questions.explanation: Net income is the amount remaining after deductions like taxes have been subtracted from gross income, representing what is actually available for spending or saving.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A financial plan that outlines expected income and planned expenditure over a specific period is called a
options: budget
house plan
ledger
consumer report
questions.explanation: A budget is a financial plan estimating expected income and allocating planned expenditure over a given period, helping guide spending decisions.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A record used to systematically track and record a family's actual income and expenses over time is called an
options: care label
house plan
advertisement
accounting ledger
questions.explanation: An accounting ledger provides an organised record of actual income and expenditure, helping families monitor their finances against their budget.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Setting aside a portion of income for future use, rather than spending it immediately, is called
options: saving
work simplification
consumer advocacy
budgeting only
questions.explanation: Saving involves deliberately setting aside income for future needs or goals, rather than spending it all immediately.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Putting money into an asset, such as property or shares, with the expectation of future financial growth is called
options: direct income
saving only
budgeting only
investment
questions.explanation: Investment involves committing money to an asset with the goal of generating future returns or growth, distinct from simple saving.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A common channel used by families to save money regularly while earning modest interest is a
options: savings account with a bank
spending all income immediately with no savings plan
unregistered informal lending scheme with no records
keeping all cash uninvested at home indefinitely
questions.explanation: A bank savings account provides a secure channel for regularly setting aside money while earning some interest over time.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A traditional cooperative savings arrangement in which members contribute a fixed amount regularly, with each member taking turns to receive the collected sum, is often called a
options: government bond only
insurance policy only
corporate share issue only
thrift and savings (esusu/ajo) scheme
questions.explanation: Traditional thrift and savings schemes (such as esusu or ajo) allow members to pool regular contributions, with each member taking turns to receive the accumulated sum.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key benefit of preparing a written family budget is that it helps
options: prevent overspending by planning expenditure against expected income
guarantee unlimited spending regardless of income
replace the need for any family income at all
eliminate the need to track any expenses
questions.explanation: A written budget helps families plan spending realistically against expected income, reducing the risk of overspending.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A family's fixed expenses, such as rent or loan repayments, are best described as costs that
options: are entirely optional and can be skipped freely
vary significantly from month to month with usage
remain the same each period, regardless of changes in usage or consumption
occur only once in a family's lifetime
questions.explanation: Fixed expenses, such as rent or loan repayments, remain constant each period, unlike variable expenses which fluctuate with usage or consumption.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A family's variable expenses, such as food or utility bills, are best described as costs that
options: never need to be included in a budget
remain exactly the same amount every single period
are always higher than fixed expenses in every family
can fluctuate from period to period depending on usage or need
questions.explanation: Variable expenses change from period to period based on actual usage or need, unlike fixed expenses which remain constant.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key step in effective time management for household tasks is to
options: avoid any form of planning or scheduling
always complete the least important tasks first
complete tasks in a completely random order
prioritise tasks according to their urgency and importance
questions.explanation: Effective time management involves prioritising tasks based on their urgency and importance, ensuring critical tasks are completed first.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Delegating household tasks among family members is a management technique used mainly to
options: share the workload and develop responsibility among family members
concentrate all tasks on a single family member exclusively
eliminate the need for any task completion at all
create unnecessary conflict within the family
questions.explanation: Delegating tasks distributes the household workload more evenly and helps develop a sense of responsibility among family members.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A family's intelligence and skills, considered part of its human resources, can be developed through
options: education, training, and practical experience
complete inactivity and avoidance of new challenges
ignoring opportunities for learning entirely
relying solely on inherited traits with no further development
questions.explanation: Human resources such as intelligence and skills can be actively developed and enhanced through education, training, and practical experience over time.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A positive attitude toward household responsibilities is considered a valuable human resource mainly because it
options: improves motivation and the overall efficiency of completing tasks
only matters for tasks performed outside the home
guarantees financial success regardless of effort
has no effect on how tasks are completed
questions.explanation: A positive attitude improves motivation and can significantly enhance the efficiency and quality of how household tasks are carried out.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Community facilities, such as public libraries, health centres, and recreational parks, are considered part of a family's
options: indirect income only
material resources
direct income only
human resources only
questions.explanation: Community facilities represent material resources that a family can access and use to support its overall wellbeing, alongside personally owned property.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: An accounting ledger used in home management typically records
options: advertisements viewed by family members
only the family's long-term investment goals
dates, descriptions, and amounts of income and expenditure
personal opinions about spending habits, with no figures
questions.explanation: A home accounting ledger systematically records the dates, descriptions, and amounts of both income received and expenses incurred.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key reason for regularly reviewing and evaluating a family's budget is to
options: avoid any changes to spending habits, regardless of outcomes
identify areas of overspending and adjust future financial plans accordingly
guarantee that no adjustments will ever be needed
eliminate the need for future budgeting entirely
questions.explanation: Regularly reviewing a budget helps identify overspending or shortfalls, allowing families to make informed adjustments to future financial plans.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Effective family financial planning generally considers both
options: only short-term needs, with no consideration of the future
short-term needs and long-term goals, such as education or retirement savings
neither short-term nor long-term financial considerations
only long-term goals, with no attention to immediate needs
questions.explanation: Sound financial planning balances immediate short-term needs with longer-term goals, such as saving for children's education or retirement.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Wise purchasing behaviour generally involves consumers
options: buying the first available item regardless of price or quality
purchasing based purely on advertising claims without verification
ignoring product labels and advertisements entirely
comparing prices, quality, and value before making a purchase decision
questions.explanation: Wise purchasing involves carefully comparing available options for price, quality, and overall value before committing to a purchase.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Consumer protection agencies exist mainly to
options: increase the profit margins of manufacturers exclusively
safeguard buyers from exploitation, unsafe products, and unfair trade practices
eliminate competition between different businesses
prevent consumers from making any purchases at all
questions.explanation: Consumer protection agencies exist to protect buyers from exploitation, unsafe goods, and unfair or deceptive trade practices.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: The Nigerian regulatory agency primarily responsible for the safety and quality of food and drugs is
options: CBN
SON
NAFDAC
INEC
questions.explanation: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) regulates the safety and quality of food, drugs, and related products in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: The Nigerian regulatory agency primarily responsible for setting and enforcing general product quality standards is
options: SON (Standards Organisation of Nigeria)
INEC
CBN
NAFDAC
questions.explanation: SON develops and enforces quality standards for products manufactured or sold in Nigeria, helping protect consumers from substandard goods.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Reading and understanding product labels before purchase helps consumers mainly to
options: avoid comparing products with one another
make informed decisions about ingredients, quality, and safety
increase the price paid for the product
ignore all information about the product entirely
questions.explanation: Product labels provide important information about ingredients, usage instructions, and safety, helping consumers make informed purchasing decisions.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Advertisements should generally be evaluated by consumers with a degree of
options: critical judgement, verifying claims rather than accepting them uncritically
total disregard, without ever considering the product advertised
indifference to the accuracy of any information presented
complete, unquestioning trust in every claim made
questions.explanation: Wise consumers approach advertisements critically, verifying claims through independent research rather than accepting marketing statements at face value.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key factor to consider when choosing a house to live in is its
options: colour of the exterior paint alone
the brand of the front door alone
location, structural condition, and cost relative to the family's budget
the number of neighbouring houses only
questions.explanation: Key considerations in choosing a house include its location (proximity to work, schools, amenities), structural soundness, and affordability.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A house plan is best described as a
options: schedule of house maintenance tasks only
record of the house's purchase price only
scaled drawing showing the layout of rooms and spaces within a building
list of building materials used only
questions.explanation: A house plan is a scaled architectural drawing illustrating the arrangement and dimensions of rooms and spaces within a building.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key principle of interior design concerned with how furniture, walls, and open spaces are arranged within a room is called
options: space allocation
lighting only
ventilation only
colour selection only
questions.explanation: Space allocation considers how furniture and open areas are arranged within a room to optimise function, flow, and comfort.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key principle of interior design concerned with choosing hues that create a desired mood or complement a room's function is called
options: furniture arrangement only
ventilation only
colour selection
space allocation only
questions.explanation: Colour selection involves choosing hues that create a desired atmosphere and complement the intended use of a room.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key principle of interior design concerned with positioning furniture to balance function, traffic flow, and appearance is called
options: space allocation only
lighting only
furniture arrangement
colour selection only
questions.explanation: Furniture arrangement considers how pieces are positioned to support the room's function, allow comfortable movement, and create visual balance.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key principle of interior design concerned with the natural or artificial illumination provided within a room is called
options: lighting
colour selection only
ventilation only
space allocation only
questions.explanation: Lighting design considers both natural and artificial illumination sources, affecting a room's mood, function, and visual comfort.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key principle of interior design concerned with the movement of fresh air through a room, important for comfort and health, is called
options: lighting only
furniture arrangement only
colour selection only
ventilation
questions.explanation: Ventilation ensures adequate fresh air circulation within a room, important for both comfort and healthy indoor air quality.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Items such as curtains, cushions, and rugs, used to add comfort and decorative appeal to a room, are collectively known as
options: structural fittings only
soft furnishings
ironmongery
hard furnishings only
questions.explanation: Soft furnishings, such as curtains, cushions, and rugs, add comfort, texture, and decorative appeal to interior spaces.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Before purchasing a refrigerator, an important consideration is its
options: exterior colour alone, regardless of function
energy efficiency and storage capacity relative to family needs
weight alone, regardless of capacity
brand name alone, regardless of features
questions.explanation: Energy efficiency and appropriate storage capacity are key practical considerations when selecting a refrigerator suited to a family's needs.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key safety practice when using a gas cooker at home is to
options: regularly check for gas leaks and ensure proper ventilation
store the cooker in an unventilated, sealed room
ignore the smell of gas, assuming it is not dangerous
leave the gas supply valve permanently open when not cooking
questions.explanation: Regularly checking for leaks and maintaining good ventilation are essential safety practices for households using gas cookers.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key maintenance practice for extending the life of a washing machine is to
options: avoid overloading it and follow the manufacturer's care instructions
ignore all manufacturer guidelines
leave it permanently connected to water even when not in use, with no supervision
always overload it to save time on multiple loads
questions.explanation: Avoiding overloading and following manufacturer guidelines helps extend the working life and performance of a washing machine.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Small kitchen utensils, such as knives and graters, should generally be
options: stored loosely mixed together with no organisation
left wet and unwashed after use
cleaned, dried, and stored safely after each use
left exposed to moisture indefinitely
questions.explanation: Proper cleaning, drying, and safe storage of small kitchen utensils after use helps maintain hygiene and prevent accidents or damage.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A major factor influencing the overall cost of building or purchasing a house is
options: the number of family members who will visit occasionally
its location and the quality of materials used in construction
the season in which the family plans to move in
the colour of the surrounding neighbourhood's houses
questions.explanation: Location and the quality of construction materials are major factors influencing the overall cost of a house.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Understanding a product's warranty before purchase helps a consumer mainly by
options: guaranteeing the product will never develop any fault
eliminating the need to keep the purchase receipt
reducing the actual purchase price of the item
clarifying what repairs or replacements are covered if the product fails
questions.explanation: A warranty specifies what repairs, replacements, or remedies are available if a product develops a fault, helping consumers understand their protections before a fault occurs.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: One of the basic rights of a consumer is the right to
options: safety, ensuring products purchased do not pose unreasonable harm
purchase any product regardless of its safety record
be denied any information about a product before purchase
receive false or misleading information from sellers
questions.explanation: The right to safety is a fundamental consumer right, protecting buyers from products that could cause unreasonable harm.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: One of the basic rights of a consumer is the right to
options: be denied any choice among available products
be informed, receiving accurate information needed to make a wise purchasing decision
be charged prices with no relation to product value
be deliberately misled by sellers regarding product quality
questions.explanation: The right to be informed ensures consumers receive accurate, adequate information to make well-considered purchasing decisions.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: One of the basic responsibilities of a consumer is to
options: ignore all safety instructions provided with a product
avoid ever reporting faulty or unsafe products
use products safely and according to the manufacturer's instructions
deliberately misuse products without any consequence
questions.explanation: Consumers share responsibility for using products safely and correctly, following manufacturer instructions to avoid harm or misuse.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key reason to keep receipts after making a purchase is to
options: increase the price of the item retroactively
provide proof of purchase for warranty claims, returns, or exchanges
eliminate the need for any consumer protection at all
prevent any future returns or exchanges from being processed
questions.explanation: Keeping receipts provides essential proof of purchase, often required to process warranty claims, returns, or exchanges.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Comparing unit prices (cost per standard quantity) when shopping helps consumers to
options: avoid comparing any products before purchase
identify the most economical option among different package sizes or brands
ignore price differences between similar products
always choose the most expensive option available
questions.explanation: Comparing unit prices allows consumers to accurately identify the most economical choice, even when comparing different package sizes or brands.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key factor to consider regarding a house's location is its
options: proximity to essential amenities such as schools, markets, and healthcare facilities
complete lack of access to water or electricity
distance from all forms of transportation
isolation from any form of community or infrastructure
questions.explanation: A house's proximity to essential amenities like schools, markets, and healthcare significantly affects its convenience and suitability for a family.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Before purchasing land or a house, verifying legal ownership documents is important mainly to
options: increase the total cost of the transaction unnecessarily
guarantee immediate resale value regardless of condition
eliminate the need for any future documentation
avoid disputes over rightful ownership in the future
questions.explanation: Verifying legal ownership documents before purchase helps prevent future disputes over rightful ownership of the property.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A house's structural integrity refers mainly to
options: the soundness and safety of its physical construction
the style of furniture placed within it
the number of visitors it typically receives
the colour scheme used for interior decoration
questions.explanation: Structural integrity concerns the physical soundness and safety of a building's construction, a critical factor when choosing a house.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Natural lighting in a room, provided through windows, is generally preferred where possible mainly because it
options: reduces reliance on artificial lighting and can improve mood and wellbeing
always increases household electricity costs
eliminates the need for any ventilation
has no effect on the room's atmosphere
questions.explanation: Natural lighting reduces the need for artificial light sources and can positively affect mood and general wellbeing within a home.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Selecting furniture appropriate to the size of a room is important mainly to
options: ensure the room is always completely empty
avoid overcrowding and maintain comfortable movement within the space
eliminate the need for any furniture arrangement planning
guarantee that furniture never matches the room's colour scheme
questions.explanation: Appropriately sized furniture prevents overcrowding, maintaining comfortable movement and a balanced appearance within a room.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A well-designed kitchen layout in a home should ideally
options: position all equipment far from any workflow logic
combine sleeping and cooking areas into a single undivided space
support an efficient workflow between storage, preparation, and cooking areas
eliminate the need for any storage space
questions.explanation: An effective kitchen layout, similar to the culinary work triangle principle, supports smooth movement and workflow between storage, preparation, and cooking areas.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Before purchasing a gas cooker for the home, an important safety consideration is
options: choosing the cheapest option regardless of safety features
verifying that it meets recognised safety standards and has functioning safety features
ignoring any certification or safety standard entirely
assuming all cookers are equally safe regardless of brand
questions.explanation: Verifying that a gas cooker meets recognised safety standards helps ensure safer operation and reduces the risk of accidents in the home.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Regular servicing and cleaning of major household appliances, such as refrigerators and cookers, helps to
options: eliminate the need for any future maintenance
increase the risk of malfunction over time
extend their working lifespan and maintain efficient performance
shorten their working lifespan intentionally
questions.explanation: Regular servicing and cleaning helps extend the working lifespan of household appliances and keeps them operating efficiently.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A family structure consisting of parents and their children living together, without other relatives, is called a
options: extended family
blended family
single-parent family only
nuclear family
questions.explanation: A nuclear family consists of parents and their children living as a single household unit, distinct from extended family arrangements.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A family structure that includes parents, children, and other relatives such as grandparents, uncles, or aunts living together or closely connected, is called an
options: blended family
single-parent family only
nuclear family
extended family
questions.explanation: An extended family includes additional relatives beyond parents and children, such as grandparents or other relatives, often living together or maintaining close ties.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A family structure formed when parents with children from previous relationships combine to form a new family unit is called a
options: blended family
nuclear family
single-parent family only
extended family only
questions.explanation: A blended family forms when parents, each potentially bringing children from previous relationships, unite to create a new combined family unit.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Within a household, the role of providing financial support, guidance, and protection is traditionally associated with
options: no one in particular, as roles are never defined
distant relatives with no household ties
parents (or guardians) as heads of the household
young children exclusively
questions.explanation: Parents or guardians traditionally hold primary responsibility for providing financial support, guidance, and protection within a household, though roles can vary by family.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Proper disposal of solid waste in the home, such as regular refuse collection and appropriate bins, is important mainly to
options: attract pests and rodents intentionally
have no effect on household health at all
increase the accumulation of waste around the home
prevent the spread of disease and maintain a clean, healthy environment
questions.explanation: Proper solid waste disposal prevents the buildup of refuse that can attract pests and spread disease, supporting a clean, healthy home environment.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Proper disposal of liquid waste, such as through appropriate drainage systems, is important mainly to
options: have no impact on public health
increase the risk of water contamination intentionally
prevent contamination of water sources and reduce breeding grounds for disease vectors
eliminate the need for any water supply system
questions.explanation: Proper liquid waste disposal prevents contamination of clean water sources and reduces breeding grounds for disease-carrying insects like mosquitoes.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Access to a clean, safe water supply within the home is essential mainly for
options: decorative purposes only
no significant health-related purpose
increasing household expenses unnecessarily
drinking, cooking, and hygiene, preventing waterborne diseases
questions.explanation: Clean water is essential for safe drinking, cooking, and hygiene practices, directly helping to prevent waterborne diseases within the household.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Effective pest and rodent control in the home is important mainly to
options: prevent damage to property and reduce the risk of disease transmission
encourage the growth of pest populations
have no bearing on household health or safety
increase food contamination risks intentionally
questions.explanation: Pests and rodents can damage property and carry diseases, making effective control measures important for maintaining a safe, healthy home.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Basic home first-aid nursing skills, such as treating minor cuts and burns, are important mainly to
options: provide immediate care for minor injuries before further medical attention, if needed
replace the need for professional medical care in all situations
worsen minor injuries intentionally
have no practical benefit within the household
questions.explanation: Basic first-aid skills allow household members to provide immediate, appropriate care for minor injuries, and to stabilise more serious situations before professional help arrives.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Planning a hospitality event, such as a family celebration, generally involves considering
options: no advance preparation of any kind
the guest list, menu, venue, and budget in advance
inviting guests without any consideration of numbers or space
ignoring the preferences and needs of guests entirely
questions.explanation: Effective event planning considers key factors such as the guest list, menu, venue, and budget well in advance of the occasion.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A formal table setting typically includes
options: a defined arrangement of cutlery, glassware, and dishware according to the courses to be served
identical arrangements regardless of the meal being served
no defined arrangement at all
only a single plate with no other place settings
questions.explanation: Formal table settings follow established conventions for arranging cutlery, glassware, and dishware, often varying according to the specific courses to be served.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: An informal table setting, compared to a formal one, is generally
options: simpler and more relaxed, with fewer pieces of cutlery and less rigid arrangement
used exclusively for large, ceremonial banquets
identical in every respect to a formal table setting
more elaborate and rigidly structured than a formal setting
questions.explanation: Informal table settings are generally simpler and more relaxed than formal settings, using fewer utensils and less rigid arrangement.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Good serving etiquette when hosting guests generally includes
options: ignoring guests' dietary preferences entirely
serving the host before any guests, in every situation
serving food in a completely random and inconsistent manner
serving food from the left and clearing plates from the right, or following consistent local convention
questions.explanation: Traditional Western serving etiquette generally follows serving from the left and clearing from the right, though the key principle is consistent, considerate practice.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Good social manners during a shared meal generally include
options: polite conversation, appropriate table manners, and consideration for other guests
speaking with a full mouth as a sign of enjoyment
leaving the table abruptly without any acknowledgement
ignoring other guests entirely throughout the meal
questions.explanation: Good social manners at a shared meal include polite conversation, proper table manners, and general consideration and courtesy toward other guests.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key consideration when planning the menu for a hospitality event is
options: selecting a menu with no regard for the number of attendees
the dietary preferences, restrictions, and number of guests attending
ignoring guests' preferences entirely
preparing only foods the host personally dislikes
questions.explanation: Effective menu planning takes into account guests' dietary preferences, restrictions, and the total number of people attending the event.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key advantage of the nuclear family structure is that it
options: guarantees greater financial resources than any other family type
allows for closer, more direct supervision of children by their immediate parents
eliminates the need for any parental responsibility
always includes numerous extended relatives living together
questions.explanation: The nuclear family structure often allows for closer, more direct parental supervision and attention, given its smaller, more immediate household unit.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key advantage of the extended family structure is that it
options: always eliminates the need for any parental responsibility
provides additional support, such as childcare and shared resources, from wider family members
guarantees there will be no family conflict of any kind
excludes grandparents and other relatives from any involvement
questions.explanation: Extended family structures often provide valuable additional support, such as shared childcare responsibilities and pooled resources among relatives.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Within a household, the role of children generally includes
options: making all major financial decisions for the family
assisting with age-appropriate chores and respecting household rules
having no responsibilities of any kind within the home
being solely responsible for the family's income
questions.explanation: Children typically contribute to household life through age-appropriate chores and by respecting the rules and structure set within the family.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Good sanitation practices in the home include
options: avoiding any form of regular cleaning
contaminating water sources intentionally
regular cleaning, proper waste disposal, and maintaining clean water sources
allowing waste to accumulate indefinitely
questions.explanation: Good sanitation combines regular cleaning, proper waste disposal, and protection of clean water sources to maintain a healthy home environment.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A soakaway pit, used in some home sanitation systems, functions mainly to
options: allow wastewater to gradually disperse and filter into the surrounding soil
store clean drinking water for household use
act as the primary cooking area of the home
generate electricity for the home
questions.explanation: A soakaway pit allows treated wastewater to disperse gradually into the surrounding soil, a common feature of some home sanitation systems.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A basic home first-aid kit should generally include items such as
options: only sharp tools with no protective supplies
antiseptic, bandages, and adhesive plasters
expired medications only
no supplies at all, relying solely on professional help
questions.explanation: A well-stocked basic first-aid kit typically includes antiseptic, bandages, and adhesive plasters, among other essential supplies for treating minor injuries.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: When treating a minor cut at home, the first step generally recommended is to
options: avoid any form of first aid regardless of severity
apply an unclean cloth directly to the wound
ignore the wound completely without any treatment
clean the wound and stop any bleeding using gentle pressure
questions.explanation: For a minor cut, the recommended first step is to clean the wound and apply gentle pressure to control any bleeding, before further care such as bandaging.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A well-planned family celebration, such as a birthday or naming ceremony, typically requires advance consideration of
options: the budget, guest list, venue, and required materials
ignoring the preferences of family members entirely
excluding any consideration of cost
no planning at all, relying entirely on spontaneous decisions
questions.explanation: Successful family celebrations require advance planning across several areas, including budget, guest list, venue, and materials needed.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Proper etiquette when receiving guests in the home generally includes
options: showing open hostility toward invited guests
ignoring guests upon their arrival
leaving guests unattended throughout their visit
greeting them warmly and ensuring their comfort
questions.explanation: Good hospitality etiquette begins with a warm greeting and continues with attentiveness to guests' comfort throughout their visit.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A napkin at a formal table setting is generally placed
options: inside a closed drawer during the meal
to the left of the forks, or on the centre of the plate
underneath the tablecloth, out of sight
directly on the floor beside the chair
questions.explanation: In formal table settings, the napkin is conventionally placed either to the left of the forks or folded on the centre of the plate.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: At a formal dinner, cutlery is generally used
options: from the outside in, working toward the plate as each course is served
from the plate outward, in reverse of the conventional order
using only one utensil throughout the entire meal
in any random order, with no defined sequence
questions.explanation: Formal dining etiquette conventionally uses cutlery from the outside in, with each utensil corresponding to a specific course as the meal progresses.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A key aspect of good hospitality when serving guests with dietary restrictions is to
options: ask about their needs in advance and accommodate them where possible
ignore any dietary restrictions entirely
serve only foods that conflict with their known restrictions
assume all guests share identical dietary preferences
questions.explanation: Good hospitality involves proactively asking about guests' dietary needs in advance and accommodating them wherever reasonably possible.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: The primary function of the family as a social unit includes
options: providing no economic or emotional function whatsoever
providing emotional support, socialisation, and care for its members
isolating its members from all social interaction
eliminating any responsibility for child development
questions.explanation: Families serve fundamental social functions, including providing emotional support, socialisation, and care for their members throughout life.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Regular health check-ups for family members are important mainly to
options: replace the need for good sanitation practices
detect potential health issues early and maintain overall wellbeing
increase household expenses without any real benefit
have no bearing on a family's overall wellbeing
questions.explanation: Regular health check-ups help detect potential health issues early, supporting the overall health and wellbeing of family members.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Adequate home ventilation contributes to family health mainly by
options: increasing indoor pollutant levels intentionally
eliminating the need for any fresh air circulation
having no effect on indoor air quality
reducing the buildup of indoor pollutants and improving air quality
questions.explanation: Good ventilation reduces the buildup of indoor pollutants and stale air, contributing to better indoor air quality and family health.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A well-organised host, when planning a hospitality event, should ideally prepare a
options: single, vague idea with no concrete details
plan finalised only after the event has already begun
list of tasks with no consideration of time constraints
checklist of tasks and a realistic timeline leading up to the event
questions.explanation: Effective event planning benefits from a clear checklist of tasks and a realistic timeline, ensuring all preparations are completed in good time.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: Understanding basic social manners, such as saying 'please' and 'thank you', contributes to
options: increased conflict between family members and guests
no meaningful effect on social relationships
unnecessary formality with no real social benefit
positive social relationships and mutual respect among family and guests
questions.explanation: Basic social manners, such as courteous expressions, help build positive relationships and demonstrate mutual respect among family members and guests.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: The way household chores are distributed among family members can significantly affect
options: family harmony and each member's sense of shared responsibility
only the physical appearance of the home, with no other effects
only the family's financial situation, with no social impact
nothing of significance within the family dynamic
questions.explanation: How chores are distributed can meaningfully affect family harmony and how responsible each member feels for the household's overall functioning.

questions.subject: Home Management
questions.text: A family's approach to conflict resolution significantly affects
options: only the physical cleanliness of the home
only the family's financial planning process
the overall emotional wellbeing and stability of the household
nothing related to household functioning
questions.explanation: How a family resolves conflict has a significant impact on the emotional wellbeing and overall stability of the household.
